newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Wall Street jitters blunt Euro share gains.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Wall Street jitters blunt Euro share gains.

text.p: European shares surrendered some of their earlier gains when Wall Street weakened on Thursday after the lastest crop of U.S. economic data reminded traders that inflationary fears are still stalking the markets.
"Rate concerns just won't go away...the housing numbers have put pressure on the bond market," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist for Fahnestock & Co in the United States.
U.S. housing starts jumped 4.5 percent in August to a 1.525 million annual rate against a revised 1.460 million in July, the U.S. Commerce Department said.
Economists, who had expected starts to slip to 1.445 million against 1.455 million in July, said the strong figures pointed to an economy unlikely to slow dramatically in early 1997.
At the close of European business Wall Street was down 19.98 points at 5857.38.

The London stock market hit record highs on a wave of derivative-related trading during the morning, but renewed interest rate worries, Wall Street's weakness, and nervousness ahead of a key futures expiry on Friday pared the gains.

The FTSE 100 index, which pushed to a record high of 3,987.7 points on business related to Friday's FTSE 100 and mid-250 futures and options expiry, drifted back to end the day at 3,974.3 points, up 18.6 points.
"It's been a two-way pull. The housing data and Wall Street were not too hot but FTSE futures held up well," a trader said.
French shares ended up but off their highs on profit-taking after the Bank of France shaved its intervention rate by 10 basis points to 3.25 percent.
The bank's gesture, while well received, was widely expected after yesterday's 1997 budget presentation.
"It means the Bank of France did not see the budget as being a threat in terms of inflation or the franc," a French bank economist said.

The franc was at 3.4063 per mark shortly after the rate cut, lower than before the budget announcement but off the low of 3.4092 it reached on Wednesday when the government unveiled its 1997 budget. In late trade it was at 3.4029 per mark.

German shares ended slightly lower in floor trading but a touch higher in after-hours electronic trading with the market showing little inclination to move in either direction, despite data showing German August money supply growth came in above forecasts and a new business climate index showed confidence improving slightly.
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar reconquered lost ground against the mark as the robust U.S. housing starts data kept U.S. interest rate rise speculation on the boil.
It also held its own against the yen after shedding over a yen on Wenesday in the wake of a large jump in the U.S. July trade deficit.

The dollar was also supported by another attack of the yen on the mark, traders said. Mark/yen recovered initially but lost ground again as a U.S. hedge fund was said to have sold large chunks of marks. Mark/yen stood at 72.21/24, down from a high at 72.48 and from 72.26/29 at the prevous European close.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was at 1.5138 marks and 109.41 yen compared with 1.5091 marks and 109.12 yen in Europe late on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares closed up 18.6 points at 3,974.3.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index closed up 9.6 points at 2,082.33.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 1.26 at 2,624.44. In post bourse electonic trading the IBIS Dax was up 4.26 points at 2625.46.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $382.85 compared with $383.35 late on Wednesday.
